title: automation: add multi-AZ failover and restore-drill runbooks-as-code for private installer
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Added automated multi-AZ failover and restore-drill runbooks-as-code for private deployments. Includes Terraform VPC updates, Helm chart changes, installer orchestration for failover, and runbooks + CI to exercise restore drills.
description: Motivation: production private deployments require tested high-availability (multi-AZ) and repeatable disaster-recovery drills. This PR introduces runbooks-as-code and automation to perform controlled restore drills, automated failover, and rollback procedures for private installer customers. Changes include: Terraform module updates to provision multi-AZ subnets and cross-AZ route53 failover records; Helm chart changes to add graceful shutdown hooks, leader-election configuration, and readiness/priority topology constraints; installer orchestration recipes (Ansible/Make) to trigger failover and restore sequences; a new runbooks/ha/restore-drill.yaml runbook in 'runbooks-as-code' format that codifies the drill steps and smoke tests; CI workflows that run a dry-run drill in KinD/vSphere lab (when available) and a synthetic smoke-test harness. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module: add az_count, subnet groups, cross-az route53 failover records - [x] Helm: add leaderElection config, preStop hooks, podTopologySpread constraints - [x] Installer playbooks: failover, primary-election, restore-from-snapshot - [x] Runbooks-as-code: restore-drill + smoke-tests + rollback scenario - [x] CI: add drill-dryrun job and terraform/helm linting - [x] Docs: runbook run instructions and SLA implications See commits_summary, files_changed_list and review_comments below for details. This description is intentionally compact; detailed runbook is in runbooks/ha/restore-drill.yaml and docs/runbooks/ha-drill.md. Please review the smoke-test assertions and Vault/KMS integration for snapshot keys before merging.
commits_summary: 1) terraform(vpc): support multi_az subnets, az_count variable, route53 failover record; 2) helm(redwood-private): add leaderElection, preStop hooks, podTopologySpread; 3) installer: add ansible playbooks for failover and restore-drill; 4) runbooks: add runbooks-as-code restore-drill.yaml and smoke tests; 5) ci: add drill-dryrun workflow and lint jobs; 6) docs: add runbook and run instructions; 7) fix: address helm-lint issues and tweak readiness probes based on review
review_comments: Evan Martinez: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) add a dry-run toggle for the restore-drill playbook so customers can validate without touching production; (2) document required IAM/KMS permissions for snapshot restore. — Priya: added --dry-run flag and expanded docs with KMS/IAM section.

Lina Chen: helm templates look good but helm-lint caught the podTopologySpread name; suggest using topologySpreadConstraints to be k8s-native. — Priya: switched to topologySpreadConstraints and updated templates.
Mateo Alvarez: CI e2e failed on vSphere due to timing of PV attach. Can we add a retry/backoff in the smoke-test? — Priya: added retries and a 30s backoff; re-ran CI and green.
Lina Chen: can you add a short runbook snippet showing 'how to abort a running drill' for ops? — Priya: added abort procedure to docs and runbook annotations.
summary: Implements HA/DR automation for private installer: multi-AZ Terraform support, Helm readiness/leader changes, installer playbooks, runbooks-as-code to run restore drills and smoke-tests, CI coverage for drill dry-runs. Improves reliability and provides an audited, repeatable procedure for DR exercises.
